about-section.title: About me
about-section.p1: I am a software developer based in Curitiba, Brazil, with a technology degree in Systems Analysis and Development from Unicesumar and a postgraduate qualification in Software Architecture and Solutions from XP Educação. I am currently studying Electrical Engineering at Cruzeiro do Sul.
about-section.p2: As a freelancer for Veronese Maquetes, I built a commercial web application end to end, with responsive Angular interfaces, Go services, and deployment to AWS Lambda and Vercel. The work included interface design and prototyping in Figma. I now maintain the application.
about-section.p3: I develop and maintain Manga2Ink, an open-source desktop application built with Electron, React, and TypeScript. My work includes feature development, bug investigation, refactoring, documentation, and automated tests, builds, and releases. I also work on 2D and 3D CAD modeling for manufacturing.

details: Built the commercial web application end to end, with responsive Angular interfaces and Go back-end services.
Designed interfaces and prototypes in Figma and deployed the services to AWS Lambda and the front end to Vercel.
I now maintain the application in production.
Desktop application built with Electron, React, and TypeScript to organize and convert manga into digital volumes in EPUB, CBZ, and PDF formats.
Feature development, integration of processing components, architecture review, bug investigation, and refactoring.
Automated tests, builds, and cross-platform releases with GitHub Actions; project documentation and maintenance.
2D CAD modeling for cutting machines and 3D part modeling for 3D printing, including preparation and adjustment of manufacturing files.
Work at Veronese Maquetes and occasional modeling assignments for Projecta Maquetes.

terminal-portfolio.title: Terminal Portfolio
terminal-portfolio.shortDescription: My personal portfolio, built with Angular and styled as a terminal interface.
terminal-portfolio.description: This portfolio itself — an Angular 22 app styled as a terminal, with typing animations, bilingual content (EN/PT), and server-side rendering. Built with OnPush change detection throughout, a signals-based intro sequence, and a design-token system for spacing, color, and breakpoints.

maquetaria.title: Veronese Maquetes
maquetaria.shortDescription: Custom platform for a model-making business — virtual showcase and back-office management.
maquetaria.description: A commercial web application I built as a freelancer for Veronese Maquetes, with a public showcase and an administration interface. The delivery included responsive Angular interfaces, Go back-end services on AWS Lambda, a front end on Vercel, and Figma prototypes. I now maintain the application in production.

minimal-neovim.title: Minimal Neovim
minimal-neovim.shortDescription: A modern, modular Neovim configuration optimized for productivity and aesthetics. Built with Lua.
minimal-neovim.description: A personal Neovim configuration built to be read, not just installed — favoring native APIs over plugins wherever that's enough. Treesitter and native LSP with Mason handle languages (Lua, JS/TS, Go, Python, and more), with Telescope for fuzzy finding and Neo-tree for browsing files.

gomodoro.title: Gomodoro
gomodoro.shortDescription: A lightning-fast CLI Pomodoro timer for developers, built in Go.
gomodoro.description: A terminal Pomodoro timer in Go: four work sessions with short breaks and a long one after the fourth, plus desktop notifications, audio alerts, and pause/resume/skip. Configured through a sandboxed Lua interpreter, with alert tones generated in memory so the binary has no external dependencies.

voting-system.title: Voting System
voting-system.shortDescription: Real-time voting system for competency assessments, built for Signo Tech.
voting-system.description: A real-time polling system built for Signo Tech's competency assessments: create polls, vote, and watch results update live over WebSockets. Polls track their status, and voting is blocked once a poll closes or for unauthenticated users. Angular frontend, separate backend API.

chmod-calculator.title: Chmod Calculator
chmod-calculator.shortDescription: Simple chmod calculator using only JS, HTML, and CSS.
chmod-calculator.description: A small tool for translating between symbolic (rwxr-xr--) and numeric (754) chmod permission formats — built with plain JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, no framework, as a focused exercise in DOM manipulation without any build tooling in the way.

xp-bootcamp.title: Bootcamp challenge - XP
xp-bootcamp.shortDescription: RESTful API built for a postgraduate bootcamp challenge in software architecture.
xp-bootcamp.description: A RESTful API for a software architecture postgraduate bootcamp challenge, covering auth, users, products, and orders with full CRUD. Layered as MVC with repositories and services, with InversifyJS for dependency injection and DTOs at the boundary. Express, MariaDB, and Docker Compose.

itau-challenge.title: Itaú Unibanco - Challenge
itau-challenge.shortDescription: REST API that ingests transactions and returns statistics over them — a challenge from Itaú Unibanco.
itau-challenge.description: A REST API built for an Itaú Unibanco coding challenge: it ingests financial transactions and returns statistics computed over them within a rolling time window. Built in Java with Spring Boot and Gradle.

books-app.title: BooksApp
books-app.shortDescription: Book catalog app with ratings, reviews, and recommendations based on what you've read.
books-app.description: The frontend for a book catalog app: browsing, ratings, reviews, and recommendations based on what a user has read, plus JWT login/signup and profiles. Built with React and React Router, Context API instead of Redux to keep it simple, SCSS modules, and Axios against a separate API.

airlock-rest.title: Airlock REST
airlock-rest.shortDescription: REST API refactored to Clean Architecture, with JWT auth and test coverage via Jest.
airlock-rest.description: A REST API first built following an Apollo Server/GraphQL course, then refactored into Clean Architecture as an exercise in separating concerns: domain, application, and infrastructure layers. TypeScript, Express, and MariaDB, with bcrypt and JWT for auth and Jest tests written test-first.

portfolio.title: First Portfolio
portfolio.shortDescription: My first personal portfolio, built with Solid.js.
portfolio.description: My first personal portfolio, and my first project with Solid.js after coming from React — built to learn Solid's fine-grained reactivity model firsthand instead of just reading about it. TypeScript throughout, bundled with Vite, containerized with Docker.

tic-tac-toe.title: Tic-Tac-Toe
tic-tac-toe.shortDescription: Tic-Tac-Toe in C# — play locally against a friend or against a Minimax-powered AI.
tic-tac-toe.description: A Tic-Tac-Toe implementation in C# with two modes: local two-player splitscreen, or against a bot. The bot plays via the Minimax algorithm, walking the full game tree to always pick an optimal move rather than relying on heuristics.

todo-list.title: Todo List
todo-list.shortDescription: Simple task management app with a React front-end and Node.js back-end.
todo-list.description: A task management app split into a Node.js API and a React frontend, in a monorepo with separate api and client directories. Covers create/edit/delete for tasks with persistent storage and JWT-based authentication, with a seed command for populating initial data.

json-visual-editor.title: JSON Visual Editor
json-visual-editor.shortDescription: Browser-based visual editor for importing, editing, comparing, and exporting JSON files without hand-editing raw syntax.
json-visual-editor.description: A browser-based JSON editor for editing structured data visually — forms for objects, tables or cards for arrays — instead of raw text. Includes global search, 50-step undo/redo, a structural diff against the original file, and local autosave. Vue 3 and strict TypeScript, entirely client-side: files never leave the browser.

mangabind.title: Mangabind
mangabind.shortDescription: Groups chapter-by-chapter manga downloads into one .cbz per volume, ready for a reader or converter.
mangabind.description: A Go command-line tool that groups manga chapters downloaded one by one — loose folders and .cbz files with inconsistent naming — into one .cbz per volume, or one archive for the whole series. Pluggable parsing strategies resolve the names, and a dry run previews the grouping first. The grouping step behind mangaprep and Manga2Ink.

manga2ink.title: Manga2Ink
manga2ink.shortDescription: Desktop app for organizing manga chapters into volumes and converting them into books for your e-reader.
manga2ink.description: An open-source desktop application for organizing manga chapters into volumes and converting them to EPUB, CBZ, and PDF. Built with Electron, React, and TypeScript, it integrates Mangabind and mangaprep for local processing and supports sharing books with KOReader over the local network. I develop and maintain the project, including architecture review, bug investigation, refactoring, documentation, and automated tests, builds, and cross-platform releases with GitHub Actions. In alpha.

mangaprep.title: mangaprep
mangaprep.shortDescription: Rust command-line tool that converts manga into EPUB, CBZ, or PDF books sized for your e-reader.
mangaprep.description: A standalone Rust command-line tool that converts manga into EPUB, CBZ, or PDF books for e-readers: it crops margins, sizes pages for the screen, adjusts contrast, and handles double-page spreads, with profiles for Kindle, Kobo, and reMarkable. Follows Kindle Comic Converter's image processing as an independent implementation.

rv-wheel.title: RVWheel
rv-wheel.shortDescription: Open-source racing wheel driver support for a game via UE4SS, built in C++ with DirectInput and force feedback.
rv-wheel.description: RV There Yet? has no native racing wheel support, so this adds it from outside via UE4SS, without touching the game's executable. Handles hot-plugged DirectInput devices, JSON device profiles matched by VID/PID, guided calibration, and optional force feedback with safety limits. C++20 with CMake, vcpkg, and 231+ Catch2 tests.

dotfiles.title: Dotfiles
dotfiles.shortDescription: Personal Arch Linux and Hyprland dotfiles, with dedicated setups for desktop, notebook, and WSL.
dotfiles.description: My own Arch Linux setup, split across three branches: a full Hyprland desktop, a notebook profile tuned for touchpad gestures and power management, and a terminal-only WSL2 setup. An install.sh pulls packages via yay and symlinks everything into place.

cisc-smart-home.title: CISC Smart Home
cisc-smart-home.shortDescription: An ESP32 smart home scale model with gas and humidity monitoring, automation, and mobile access.
cisc-smart-home.description: CISC — Casa Inteligente Segura e Confortável (Safe and Comfortable Smart Home) — is a home automation system demonstrated through a physical scale model. In the kitchen, an MQ-2 sensor detects gas leaks, closes the valve, and triggers an alarm; a physical button resets the system once gas levels return to normal. In the bedroom, a DHT11 sensor monitors temperature and humidity and enables automatic or manual dehumidifier control. An Android app connected to the ESP32's own Wi-Fi network brings together readings, history, controls, and alerts, without requiring internet access or a router. Communication uses REST and SSE events, while safety rules run directly on the ESP32. An academic electrical and electronic systems project, with C++ firmware and a KiCad circuit schematic.

imperial-to-si-converter.title: Imperial to SI Converter
imperial-to-si-converter.shortDescription: A Python and Textual unit converter with a terminal interface, keyboard shortcuts, and mouse support.
imperial-to-si-converter.description: An academic Modeling I project for an Electrical Engineering course, converting length, mass, volume, and temperature from Imperial units to SI. The Textual interface supports keyboard navigation with Vim-style shortcuts as well as mouse interaction, and updates results while typing. Conversion logic is separate from the interface, with tests and a registry of converters by measurement type. PyInstaller can package it as a standalone executable. The gallery images are the screenshots published in the project README.
